target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): prevent mid-transcript [cron:] from wiping archive content
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user message starts with `[cron:...]` (e.g., pasting a cron log line), `buildSessionEntry` classifies the entire session as cron-generated and wipes all previously collected archive content. The whole transcript becomes invisible to `memory_search`.

Real cron prompts are always the first message. User-typed `[cron:]` text appears mid-conversation.

Closes #98241

## Fix

Add `collected.length === 0` guard to the cron classification wipe in `buildSessionEntry`.  The wipe now only applies to the first message — real cron sessions still work, mid-transcript `[cron:]` no longer destroys prior context.

**1 line, 2 files (+ test)**

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — mid-transcript [cron:] survives

```
node --import tsx -e "... import { buildSessionEntry } ..."

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  #98241 Real Proof — mid-transcript [cron:]
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  User: Remember: vendor is Acme, budget 5000
  Assistant: Got it.
  Acme: ✅
  budget 5000: ✅
  ✅ PASS — archive content survives
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

Real `buildSessionEntry` called with a `.reset.` archive file containing 3 messages where the third starts with `[cron:...]`. Prior content ("Acme", "budget 5000") survives the cron classification.

### Test suite

```
pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)    Tests  38 passed (38)
```

### Formatting & lint

```
pnpm exec oxfmt --check ...  (pass)
git diff --check  (clean)
```

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] memory-host-sdk (session indexing)

## Security Impact

- New permissions? No
- Secrets handling changed? No
- New network calls? No
